job.title: Health and Safety Business Partner

job.title: Return to Work Coordinator
job.description:
About Them
Our client is a leading, ASX-listed restaurant operator with a national footprint and a large, diverse workforce. Based in Hamilton, their Brisbane support office brings together the teams that support restaurant operations across Australia. You’ll join a supportive safety and wellbeing team that takes a practical, people-focused approach to helping injured employees recover and return to work.

The opportunity
Supporting a national portfolio, predominantly across Queensland, you will help coordinate workers’ compensation claims and suitable duties arrangements. Your responsibilities will include:
  • Providing claim forms and guiding team members through the lodgement process.
  • Following up paperwork, answering questions and keeping claims progressing.
  • Developing, updating and monitoring suitable duties plans.
  • Supporting team members and managers throughout the return to work process.
  • Maintaining accurate and confidential records.
Most existing claims already have suitable duties plans in place. You will have guidance and support from your manager, with minimal insurer engagement and no direct doctor or rehabilitation provider liaison expected during this assignment.

About you
You bring experience in return to work or injury management, sound workers’ compensation knowledge and a Queensland Rehabilitation and Return to Work Coordinator qualification.

You are organised, empathetic and comfortable picking up the phone to support people and follow things through. Confidence learning new systems is essential; experience with the business’s specific platform is not required.

Interested?
Apply now or contact Keilee Armstrong at The Safe Step on karmstrong@thesafestep.com.au for a confidential discussion.

job.title: HSEQ Project Manager

Sitting as part of the Project Senior Management Team, this is much more than a traditional site safety role. You will lead HSEQ across the project, providing direction across safety, quality, assurance, contractor management and operational risk from mobilisation through construction, fit out and commissioning.

The Role
Leading a dedicated project Safety and Quality team, your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading HSEQ performance across the project
  • Providing visible leadership across a large construction workforce
  • Leading and developing project safety and quality resources
  • Driving risk management, assurance and governance
  • Partnering with project leaders and contractors to improve WHSEQ performance
  • Providing oversight of quality processes across complex electrical construction and fit out
  • Supporting HSEQ systems, processes and continuous improvement
  • Contributing as a key member of the senior project leadership team
About You
We are looking for an established HSEQ professional with experience across major construction, electrical, engineering or infrastructure projects.
You will ideally bring:
  • Strong project based safety leadership experience
  • Exposure to electrical construction, fit out or complex building services

  • Genuine Quality and assurance capability
  • Experience leading HSEQ or project safety teams
  • Strong contractor and stakeholder management capability
  • The credibility to influence senior project and operational leaders
Electrical construction experience would be highly regarded, particularly across large commercial builds, complex electrical installations or highly serviced facilities.

job.title: Work Health and Safety Coordinator I AHCSA
job.description:
About the organisation
As the health voice for Aboriginal people in South Australia, AHCSA advocates for communities and our Member Services, supporting the delivery of culturally appropriate health programs grounded in a holistic understanding of health and wellbeing.
  
“Our Health, Our Choice, Our Way” is at the heart of AHCSA's identity, reflecting its commitment to Aboriginal self-determination, cultural safety and strengthening the Aboriginal community-controlled health sector.  Guided by the principle of Aboriginal health in Aboriginal hands, AHCSA is committed to supporting Aboriginal people and communities to have a voice in decisions affecting their health and wellbeing.
  
About the opportunity
AHCSA is seeking an experienced Work Health and Safety professional to lead and strengthen its approach to workplace health, safety and wellbeing.
  
This is an opportunity to make a genuine difference in an organisation where psychological safety, cultural respect and employee wellbeing are just as important as legislative compliance.
  
Working across the organisation and with Member Services, you will build relationships, develop capability and ensure WHS practices are practical, accessible and responsive to the needs of AHCSA's people.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Lead the development, implementation and continuous improvement of AHCSA's WHS Management System, policies and procedures.
  • Manage WHS governance, risk assessments, audits, incident investigations and regulatory compliance.
  • Identify and manage psychosocial hazards, strengthening psychological safety and workplace wellbeing.
  • Embed cultural safety principles into WHS practices, recognising the importance of cultural identity, lived experience and community.
  • Chair the WHS Committee and provide advice and guidance to senior leaders and employees.
  • Coordinate WHS training, inductions, reporting and Return to Work activities.
  • Build capability and encourage employee engagement in workplace health and safety.
About you
You will bring sound technical WHS knowledge and experience, together with the interpersonal skills, cultural awareness and judgement to work effectively within AHCSA.
  
You are approachable, a good listener and someone who takes the time to build genuine relationships and understand different perspectives. You recognise that creating a safe workplace goes beyond policies and procedures, and that trust, respect and open communication are fundamental to achieving positive outcomes.
  
You will bring:
  • Experience or demonstrated capability in psychosocial risk management, psychological safety and workplace wellbeing.
  • The ability to engage respectfully with Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal employees, leaders and stakeholders.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to provide advice and constructively challenge when required.
  • A practical, collaborative approach to problem-solving, continuous improvement and building WHS capability.
  
A Diploma of Work Health and Safety, or Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety with substantial demonstrated experience at coordinator level, is essential.
  
Experience within community cantered environment will be highly regarded.
  
Why join AHCSA?
AHCSA offers the opportunity to contribute to an organisation making a meaningful difference to Aboriginal health and wellbeing across South Australia.
  
Along with a supportive, culturally respectful and purpose-driven workplace, benefits include:
  • Generous not-for-profit salary packaging.
  • Two additional weeks of paid leave over the Christmas period.
  • Four weeks of annual leave with 17.5% leave loading.
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Flexible working arrangements and professional development support.
  
How to apply
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are strongly encouraged to apply.

Cultural knowledge, lived experience and community connections are recognised and valued.

Applications are also welcomed from people of all backgrounds who demonstrate the experience, cultural awareness and commitment to AHCSA's values required for this position.
  
To apply, please submit your resume and a covering letter outlining your interest and relevant experience.

job.title: Health & Safety Systems and Assurance Specialist
job.description:
Sydney | Permanent | National Scope

About Them
Our client is a highly successful Australian market leader with a long standing history and a reputation for operational excellence. Employing thousands of people across a diverse portfolio of businesses, they continue to invest in their people, systems and health and safety capability to support sustainable growth.
As part of a well regarded national health and safety team, this newly focused specialist role will play an important part in strengthening health and safety systems, governance and assurance across the organisation.

About the Role
Reporting to the Systems & Governance Manager, the Health & Safety Systems & Assurance Specialist will lead the ongoing development, implementation and improvement of the organisation's WHS Management System and health and safety assurance framework. 
This is a hands on technical role for someone who enjoys making safety systems clear, practical and effective. You will work closely with health and safety, operational, risk, audit and other key stakeholders to ensure WHS requirements are well designed, understood and effectively implemented across the business. 
A significant part of the role will also focus on assurance, including shaping the annual audit and assurance program, reviewing the effectiveness of risk controls and supporting improvements in how health and safety performance is monitored and reported. 

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for:
  • Leading the development, implementation and continuous improvement of the WHS Management System
  • Developing clear and practical WHS documentation aligned with legislative requirements, Codes of Practice and relevant industry standards
  • Maintaining the WHS system review program and supporting consultation on new and changing requirements
  • Monitoring legislative and industry changes and translating these into practical business requirements
  • Leading the development and implementation of the health and safety assurance plan
  • Establishing annual audit and assurance activities informed by risk profiles and WHS performance
  • Leading internal WHS audits and verification activities where required
  • Reviewing the effectiveness of health and safety risk controls, including critical risk controls
  • Supporting operational teams in the practical application of WHS system and compliance requirements.
About You
We are looking for an experienced health and safety professional with strong technical capability across WHS management systems, risk and assurance.
Ideally, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience developing, writing and implementing WHS management systems
  • Strong knowledge of WHS risk management and assurance, including assurance frameworks and risk reviews
  • Experience with audit and verification activities and an understanding of risk control effectiveness
  • Excellent technical writing skills with the ability to make complex requirements clear and practical
  • The ability to interpret data and apply insights within an operational environment
  • Experience or strong capability across WHS technology, data and analytics
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to coach and build WHS capability
  • A relevant qualification in safety, risk or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
  • Lead Auditor qualifications would be highly regarded.
Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an opportunity to take ownership of meaningful systems and assurance work across a large and diverse operational organisation. Rather than simply maintaining an established system, you will have the opportunity to influence how WHS requirements are structured, applied, assured and continuously improved across the business.
The role will suit someone who enjoys getting into the detail of systems and assurance, but can also step back and understand how those systems need to work in a practical operational environment.

If you are an experienced WHS systems, governance or assurance professional looking for a technically interesting role with broad organisational reach, we would welcome a application or a confidential discussion.

job.title: Group Risk and Retail Protections Manager

With a long history of success, the organisation continues to invest in innovation, technology, and operational excellence to support its next phase of growth. Its collaborative and high-performing culture encourages fresh thinking, continuous improvement, and strong leadership, creating an environment where people are empowered to make a meaningful impact.

You will bring:
